## Reusable rules

1. **Model polymorphic variants with explicit discriminators** Use a discriminated base and typed variants when clients need to distinguish payload shapes; plain unions of models can become untyped SDK values. Retain string extensibility where the contract intentionally allows future values. *Scope:* TypeSpec request and response polymorphism, especially SDK-facing models *Explicit reviewer guidance.* Evidence: https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46314#discussion_r4084437343, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/53874d1b6d1e898de87112fecba43b966fc3de0e/specification/ai-foundry/data-plane/Foundry/src/agents-optimization/inputs.tsp, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/53874d1b6d1e898de87112fecba43b966fc3de0e/specification/ai-foundry/data-plane/Foundry/src/agents-optimization/routes.tsp

2. **Make SDK-visible contracts match supported behavior** Use established job helpers and type query parameters to reflect actual serialization and supported values. Keep pagination, expansion, defaults, and constraints grounded in the service behavior rather than exposing misleading or unsupported schema options. *Scope:* TypeSpec routes and models for data-plane operations *Explicit reviewer guidance.* Evidence: https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46314#discussion_r4084437332, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46314#discussion_r4084437338, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46314#discussion_r4009631075, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46314#discussion_r4009685642, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/53874d1b6d1e898de87112fecba43b966fc3de0e/specification/ai-foundry/data-plane/Foundry/src/agents-optimization/routes.tsp

3. **Choose collection shapes for their cardinality and semantics** A small fixed set can use named properties; dynamic unique keys with uniform values can use a dictionary. Prefer arrays when entries need per-item metadata or multiple values can occur. The final contract retained stage/model-attributed usage arrays rather than flattening them. *Scope:* TypeSpec result and estimate models *Explicit reviewer guidance.* Evidence: https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46314#discussion_r4010033918, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46314#discussion_r4019436725, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46314#discussion_r4019436961, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/53874d1b6d1e898de87112fecba43b966fc3de0e/specification/ai-foundry/data-plane/Foundry/src/agents-optimization/jobs.tsp, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/53874d1b6d1e898de87112fecba43b966fc3de0e/specification/ai-foundry/data-plane/Foundry/src/agents-optimization/inputs.tsp

4. **Avoid redundant inherited properties, but preserve discriminator literals** Do not redeclare ordinary inherited properties such as an error field. A subtype may repeat a discriminator as a literal value when needed to identify the concrete variant to TypeSpec and generated SDKs. *Scope:* TypeSpec model inheritance and discriminated subtype definitions *Inferred lesson.* Evidence: https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46314#discussion_r4019437234, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46314#discussion_r4019437754, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/53874d1b6d1e898de87112fecba43b966fc3de0e/specification/ai-foundry/data-plane/Foundry/src/agents-optimization/jobs.tsp

5. **Check generated-language naming conventions** A TypeSpec model name can fail language-specific validation; rename it or apply a language-scoped client name override. Keep SDK customizations aligned with the final model/property structure rather than assuming a wire-name change is needed. *Scope:* TypeSpec models and per-language SDK client customizations *Explicit reviewer guidance.* Evidence: https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46314#discussion_r4084437327, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/53874d1b6d1e898de87112fecba43b966fc3de0e/specification/ai-foundry/data-plane/Foundry/src/agents-optimization/inputs.tsp, https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/53874d1b6d1e898de87112fecba43b966fc3de0e/specification/ai-foundry/data-plane/Foundry/src/sdk-java-azure-ai-agents/client.tsp

## Caveats

- The initial review proposed a separate evaluation outcome alongside termination reason; later discussion said termination reason should be used with outcome, while the frozen patch exposes termination_reason in the result and the inherited JobLike status, not a separate evaluation_outcome field. The advice therefore remains unresolved as to whether candidate-search outcomes need another field.
- A reviewer asked for integer call-count bands, but the author stated expected call counts may be fractional; the frozen source retains float64 estimate bands. This is a service-specific estimation decision, not a universal numeric-type rule.
- The frozen source sets inline dataset limits to 2000, while a later comment reports service limits of 500 for validation and 2000 for training and asks whether to use the conservative value. No evidence resolves that service/schema discrepancy; reported service compatibility is not proof of schema compatibility.
- Duration feedback is context-dependent: the final source uses FoundryDurationMilliseconds for millisecond values, while Java duration overrides for a removed seconds-based field were deleted. Do not infer one encoding rule for every duration.
- The PR description and bot comments are process boilerplate; APIView links and pipeline statements are attributed reports. No tests were run by this extraction.
